rows.basis: Revenue of the Data Centers line, 1,112.1M of 3,181.1M net sales; HVAC Technologies, Heat Transfer Solutions and Performance Technologies are excluded. Data center, not AI; it is reported as a product group inside Climate Solutions in the FY2026 release and becomes a separate segment in FY2027.

Revenue of the Data Centers line, 644.2M of 2,583.5M. This matches the release's 'Data center revenue increased 119% to $644 million', which includes 197M from the Scott Springfield acquisition. Data center, not AI.

Revenue of the Data Centers line, 294.2M of 2,407.8M. The release says data center revenue grew 69%. This is a product-group disaggregation inside Climate Solutions, not a reported segment. Data center, not AI.
Revenue of the Data center cooling product line, 173.8M of 2,297.9M. This is a disaggregation inside Climate Solutions, not a reported segment. Data center, not AI.
The MD&A says sales to data center customers increased $32 million. That is an increment, not a revenue level, and no data-center revenue line is in the pack for FY2022. Data center, not AI.

The FY2026 release and the Q1 FY2027 release both expect Data Center sales to grow 60 to 80% in FY2027, with no dollar amount. The $4B hyperscale chiller agreement is an agreement, not revenue, and is not in the pack. Data center, not AI.
Company target of $2 billion of Data Center revenue by fiscal 2028, which the Q3 FY2026 release says it is 'solidly ahead of'. This is a target, not a forecast of total revenue. Data center, not AI.

The MD&A and the release tie higher FY2026 capex (143.3M total) to Data Centers manufacturing expansion in the U.S. and Canada, with no amount. Climate Solutions segment capex of 113.4M also includes HVAC Technologies, so it is not an AI line and is not used.
The FY2024 MD&A and release plan added data center cooling capacity in the US, Canada and the UK (a new UK site was purchased), with no amount.
The Q2 FY2025 release says Modine continues to expand manufacturing capacity for colocation and hyperscale customers, with no amount.

A $100M Data Centers capacity expansion in North America: a new Dallas facility, further expansion in Grenada MS, and two repurposed Performance Technologies sites. It is a program amount whose spend may fall across FY2026 and FY2027. Data center, not AI.
The releases cite SG&A growth from 'data center growth investment' and gross-margin pressure from capacity-expansion costs for data center products, with no amounts.
